blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Policy Distillation**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Trajectory Fine-Tuning, § Policy Distillation
blocks.md: Consider an automated repair agent whose system prompt carries a detailed debugging checklist and worked examples showing how to inspect a stack trace before revising a tool call. In production, the agent resends this entire prompt prefix on every turn of every trajectory, consuming context-window capacity and raising time-to-first-token latency even though the procedural workflow belongs in the weights under a later section. Training the model to internalize the procedure lets the runtime drop the checklist from the prompt and reclaim those tokens on every call.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Context distillation
- Teacher distillation

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Trajectory distillation matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A costly teacher configuration generates trajectories that pass the same admission as any demonstration, so distillation from sampled tokens is imitation rather than soft-target matching.

questions.q: The section **Policy Distillation** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Loss is placed only on selected policy-response positions while prompts, refused proposals, and observations stay as attended context with zero loss, because a trajectory has two authors and only one is trained.
Loss values are comparable only under identical split, serialization, mask, and normalization, and promotion requires closed-loop task acceptance under the serving configuration, not lower loss.
A costly teacher configuration generates trajectories that pass the same admission as any demonstration, so distillation from sampled tokens is imitation rather than soft-target matching.
Token averaging and example averaging weight trajectories differently, so segmentation and microbatching silently re-weight the corpus unless the normalization rule is fixed.
questions.hint: Re-read the excerpt and the section map: which idea is this section building toward?
questions.explanation: This section develops **Trajectory distillation**: A costly teacher configuration generates trajectories that pass the same admission as any demonstration, so distillation from sampled tokens is imitation rather than soft-target matching.

points: You have worked through Policy Distillation.
